System Integrity and Event Monitoring
Secure Internet and Endpoint Management
Security Incident Escalation Model
questions.explain: SIEM stands for Security Information and Event Management -- the platform that centralizes, correlates, and alerts on log data.

questions.q: Which of a SIEM's four core functions involves combining events across different sources to detect a pattern that no single log would reveal on its own?
options: Retention
Correlation
Centralization
Licensing
questions.explain: Correlation is the function that ties events from different sources together to surface a pattern, like a port scan followed by an antivirus alert on the same target.

questions.q: In the port-scan-then-AV-alert example, why do the two log entries matter more together than they do separately?
options: Neither log entry is ever recorded unless both occur
On their own, each is easy to dismiss as noise; correlated together by IP and timing, they form a single working incident
Only the antivirus alert is ever worth investigating
The two entries are unrelated and correlating them is a false positive by definition
questions.explain: A port scan and an isolated AV alert each look unremarkable alone. A SIEM's correlation engine links them by source IP and timing into one incident worth investigating.

questions.q: Why do SOCs care about log retention beyond just having convenient storage?
options: Retention has no real practical purpose beyond saving disk space
Forensic investigations often happen long after an incident, and compliance frameworks like PCI-DSS and HIPAA require logs to be kept for a defined minimum period
Retention is only required for logs that triggered an alert
Logs older than 24 hours are legally required to be deleted
questions.explain: Retention supports after-the-fact forensic investigation and satisfies compliance mandates that require logs to be kept for a set period.

questions.q: What is the main thing that distinguishes a SIEM from simply storing all your logs in one central place?
options: A SIEM uses more expensive hardware
A SIEM actively correlates and alerts on patterns across sources in real time, rather than just holding data for someone to search later
There is no real distinction -- any centralized log storage is a SIEM
A SIEM only works with logs from a single vendor
questions.explain: Centralized storage alone is passive. A SIEM adds real-time correlation and alerting on top of that storage, which is what makes it a SIEM rather than just a log repository.
